:::{#exm-proof}
#### The sum of two even integers is even

Let $a$ and $b$ be even integers ([definition](number-systems.qmd#def-even-odd)).
Then $a = 2j$ and $b = 2k$ for some integers $j$ and $k$, and

$$
\ba
a + b
&= 2j + 2k
&& \text{(substitute } a = 2j \text{ and } b = 2k \text{)}
\\
&= 2(j + k)
&& \text{(distributive law)}
\ea
$$

The second line uses the [distributive law](algebra.qmd#def-distributive).
Since $j + k$ is an integer, $a + b$ is even ([definition](number-systems.qmd#def-even-odd)).
For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 + 10 &= 2 \cd 2 + 2 \cd 5 \\
&= 2 \cd 7 \\
&= 14.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
